docs.title: 🛡️ SATGuardian — The WAF That Can Prove Its Work
docs.text:
Deterministic, auditable security decision layer. Not another WAF — the engine that decides why a request is malicious, bit by bit, before any scoring-based firewall has to guess.

Status: SATGuardian Edge WAF v0.3.0. Detection has been measured on project-authored corpora — see Project Status for the evidence and its limits, including the honest statement that no third-party evaluation exists yet.

SATGuardian Edge WAF is a self-hosted deterministic security decision layer written in Rust. It evaluates security logic with 128-bit integer bitmasks (u128) in ~0.5 ms in memory, and every block is a reproducible Boolean proof — not an anomaly score. It can — only if you turn it on — send recorded anomalies to SATGuardian cloud synthesis for review.

The product promise: free, you get local protection; paying, you get ongoing review, update proposals and explanations — without ever giving up control of your WAF. Cloud review is opt-in (auto_sync_enabled defaults to false) and what it returns is stored as a proposal: nothing enters the running rule set until you approve it.

docs.title: 🎯 Why SATGuardian
docs.text:
SATGuardian is not positioned as "another WAF". It is a deterministic decision layer that does what signature- and scoring-based firewalls structurally cannot:

  1. Every decision is auditable, bit by bit. A block is a Boolean cube (feature_vector & mask) == expected over a 128-bit feature vector — reproducible and reviewable by an auditor without trusting a vendor's scoring internals. CRS-style engines answer "blocked, anomaly score 27"; SATGuardian answers which structural tokens, in which combination, triggered which rule.
  2. It complements your existing WAF instead of replacing it. Measured head-to-head against Aegis Community v1.1.0 (Coraza + OWASP CRS 4.25.1): on the CRS v4.30 attack suite the two engines detect 82.0% vs 80.7%, and their coverage is strongly complementary — union 92.9% recall, intersection only 69.8%. In a cascade, SATGuardian adds detection the signatures miss; alone, it adds explainability they cannot offer.
  3. Your traffic never leaves your infrastructure. No DNS redirection, no hosted gateway, no per-request fee. The only optional cloud contact is the review of recorded feature vectors — off by default, and its output arrives as proposals you approve, never as silent rule changes.
  4. Free edge, paid governance. Edge inspection is 100% free and unlimited. The paid layer is review: ongoing analysis of new patterns, update proposals and explanations.

Who this is for: teams that need to prove why a request was blocked — regulated workloads, audit-driven security programs, and operators who want a fast deterministic first stage in front of a heavier WAF. Who it is not for (yet): teams that need a managed console, TLS termination, geo-blocking or rate limiting in the same box — those live in the proxy/TLS layer in front of SATGuardian.

docs.title: 📊 Measured, not claimed
docs.text:
• Detection parity on the vendor suite: 82.0% vs Aegis+CRS 80.7% recall on the OWASP CRS v4.30 attack corpus (4,050 cases).
  • Complementary coverage: 92.9% union recall — each engine catches what the other misses.
  • False positives: 0.5% vs 22.9% on 665 pooled benign controls (project- authored corpus; partially in-sample — caveats in Project Status).
  • Latency: ~0.46 ms p50 / ~6 ms p99 in-memory, single thread, expanded rule set (re-measured 2026-11-10).

Full evidence, methodology, per-case verdicts and the replay harness: Project Status · Comparative analysis · Detection Corpus

docs.title: ⚡ Quick Start
docs.text:
Requires a Rust toolchain. Do not use the archived dist//releases/ artefacts — they predate the claim corrections and the approval gate.

git clone https://github.com/ExactorResearch/satguardian.git
cd satguardian
cargo build --release

# Terminal 0: any upstream on :3000, e.g.  python -m http.server 3000
# Terminal A: WAF proxy on :8080
./target/release/satguardian-waf proxy --listen 127.0.0.1:8080 --upstream http://127.0.0.1:3000

# Benign -> proxied (200 if upstream serves it); attack -> 403 with proof
curl -i http://localhost:8080/
curl -i "http://localhost:8080/api/users?search=1%27%20UNION%20SELECT%20*%20FROM%20users--%20%3Cscript%3Ealert(1)%3C/script%3E"

# Built-in benchmark, 10,000 requests
./target/release/satguardian-waf benchmark -r 10000

docs.title: 🛰️ Shadow mode — evaluate on real traffic without blocking
docs.text:
For pilots and design partners: run SATGuardian in monitor mode and it inspects every request, records detections and proofs in the local ledger — but never blocks. Production traffic is never touched while you measure real false-positive rates and latency:

./target/release/satguardian-waf proxy --mode monitor --listen 127.0.0.1:8080 --upstream http://127.0.0.1:3000

Same switch via mode = "monitor" in waf_config.toml or WAF_MODE=monitor. Details: Operations guide.

docs.title: 🔌 Integrations: plugs into what you already run
docs.text:
SATGuardian is not another WAF competing with your stack — it is the decision layer that plugs into what you already run:

  • Envoy · Istio · service mesh — native ext_authz sidecar (guide).
  • nginx · HAProxy · Traefik · Caddy — auth_request / forward_auth patterns mount it in front of your existing proxy, in minutes.
  • Kong · APISIX · Tyk — gateway ext-auth/plugin integration.
  • Kubernetes Gateway API · OPA — SATGuardian decides, OPA/Gatekeeper permits: "what was allowed" + "what was blocked and why".
  • Splunk · Sentinel · OpenTelemetry — every block can reach your SIEM or tracing pipeline with its Boolean proof attached.

See the full Integration Ecosystem.

docs.title: 💰 Pricing
docs.text:
• Edge WAF — free forever. Local inspection is 100% free and unlimited; no per-request charge, no traffic tax.
  • Cloud Review — from $20/mo. Ongoing analysis of new patterns, update proposals and explanations — you approve every change. Quota exhaustion pauses cloud review; local rules keep enforcing.
  • Enterprise — custom. Higher volumes, more servers, negotiated terms. 256+ variable matrices are engineering projects, not a plan.

Internal metering (Security Units) and job ceilings are documented in the technical guides — configuration · operations.

docs.title: Detection corpus and measurement protocol
docs.text: This directory contains hand-labelled HTTP requests used by tests/independent_corpus_test.rs. The corpus is small and hand-written on purpose: it exists to make regressions visible, not to certify real-world accuracy.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
File Contents Status independent_v1.json 63 attacks + 16 benign controls across SQLi, XSS, RCE, LFI, SSRF, GraphQL, prototype pollution, JWT, framework exploits, WordPress and file exposure. Regression suite after the 2026-11-01 fix pass. heldout_v1.json 17 attack variants + 4 benign controls written after the first fix pass. Measured once before correction, then kept as a regression suite. heldout_v2.json 98 attacks + 57 benign controls written on 2026-11-04, deliberately using techniques absent from the two files above, plus six attack families the engine has no name for (NoSQL, XXE, SSTI, response splitting, Host header, upload). Held out at the moment of writing. heldout_v2_report.json is its single measurement.

Payload provenance is recorded per case in the note field and in the provenance block: OWASP CRS/WSTG notes, PortSwigger filter-evasion notes, Log4Shell obfuscation catalogues, RFC 7519 JWT fixtures, and benign snippets modelled on framework/CDN documentation.

heldout_v2.json adds a constraint the earlier batches did not state: the payloads were hand-written from catalogues the author recalled rather than copied from a fetched file, so each note names the documented technique instead of a URL, and the benign set is imagined traffic — not a sample from a customer's access log. The first run is produced by tests/heldout_v2_measurement_test.rs, which asserts nothing about detection quality on purpose: a held-out estimate that fails into a fix and is then re-measured is not an estimate.

docs.title: Measurements
docs.text: All numbers below come from SatguardianSatEngine::new() with the default configuration and the corpus request as the only input. No network hop, no upstream, no stateful verdict.

Metric Value Attacks 63 Benign 16 True positives 51 False negatives 12 False positives 3 Recall 80.95% False-positive rate 18.75%

Missed attacks: MySQL executable comments hiding UNION/OR (/*!50000...*/), || tautologies, HTML-entity javascript: schemes, Java ProcessBuilder, encoded PowerShell, overlong UTF-8 traversal, \u-escaped __proto__, and nested ${lower:...} Log4Shell lookups.

False positives: a local <script src="/static/app.js"> include, a data:image/png;base64 URI, and the URL http://localhost:3000 in issue text.

Held-out first run (heldout_v1.json):

Metric Value Attacks 17 Benign 4 True positives 11 False negatives 6 False positives 0 Recall 64.71% False-positive rate 0.00%

Missed: numeric constant comparisons (OR 2>1), OR 1--, U+2215 path separators, 127.1 loopback, IPv4-mapped IPv6 loopback, and ${env:...:-j} Log4Shell lookup assembly.

docs.title: Regression run after fixes
docs.text: Both files currently report 100% recall and 0% false-positive rate in cargo test --test independent_corpus_test. These are in-sample regression numbers. Every case was used to drive the fixes above, so they say "the pinned cases still pass", not "the engine catches X% of real attacks".

docs.title: Held-out measurement, heldout_v2.json (2026-11-04)
docs.text:
One run, produced before any engine change in response to these cases. Full detail, including every miss and every blocked control, is in corpus/heldout_v2_report.json.

Metric Value Attacks 98 Benign controls 57 Detected 55 Missed 43 Controls cleared 53 Controls blocked 4 Recall 56.1% (95% CI 46.3%–65.5%) False-positive rate 7.0% (95% CI 2.8%–16.7%)

By family: XSS 12/12, GraphQL 4/4, prototype pollution 4/4, WordPress probes 5/6, path traversal 6/8, command injection 5/8, SQL injection 8/12, JWT 3/4, framework exploit probes 3/8, sensitive-file probes 3/7, SSRF 1/8, XXE 1/2, and zero detection for the five families the engine has no rules for at all: NoSQL operator injection, SSTI, HTTP response splitting, Host-header injection and malicious upload.

The four blocked controls are the honest cost of the signature set: an inline SVG in a CSS value, a password containing ;ls -la, the public /wp-json/wp/v2/posts listing, and the WordPress admin-ajax.php heartbeat — those two being the engine blocking ordinary use of the platform a customer is most likely to run.

What this number is: the first out-of-sample estimate the project has produced, on hand-written attacks and imagined traffic. What it is not: a measurement against real customer logs, a certification, or a number to put on the site without this paragraph next to it. The previous batches' 100%/0% are still only in-sample regressions.

This batch is now spent. Any engine change made to close a miss listed in heldout_v2_report.json turns heldout_v2.json into a third regression suite, and the next honest estimate has to come from a new heldout_v3 labelled before it is run.

docs.title: Later held-out batches (benchmarks/real_comparative/corpus/*.jsonl)
docs.text:
Batches v3–v10 moved to JSONL corpora under benchmarks/real_comparative/corpus/ and were each measured once, then spent as tuning inputs. Their one-shot figures remain in STATUS.md and the generated reports for provenance:

Batch One-shot result Status heldout_v3–heldout_v7 measured once each (see STATUS.md) spent; regression floors heldout_v8 77.5% recall / 4.2% FPR spent heldout_v9 50.0% recall / 6.4% FPR (heldout_v9_report.json) spent; post-repair diagnostic 97.7%/4.3% heldout_v10 one-shot frozen result / 0.0% FPR (heldout_v10_report.json, frozen); current engine 100%/0.0% (heldout_v10_post_tuning_report.json) the one-shot file is the publishable blind estimate; the 100%/0.0% file is the current-engine diagnostic on the same now-spent batch

crs_v430.jsonl is the vendor-authored OWASP CRS v4.30 suite. Coverage against it is an in-sample measurement (the engine was tuned on its misses), currently 3,321/4,050 labelled attacks (82.0% recall). It is not an independent or third-party evaluation.

docs.title: Rules for changing the corpus
docs.text:
1. Label a case before running it against the engine. Do not add a case and then label it from the engine output.
  2. Keep the note and provenance. A case without a source is not reviewable.
  3. When a case fails, fix the engine or document the gap. Do not delete the case to make the suite green.
  4. If you consume a held-out batch by tuning against it, say so here and create a new batch instead of reusing the old label.
  5. Do not publish corpus metrics as independent quality evidence. The docs/ benchmark pages must link to this file and repeat the caveat.

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
cargo test --test independent_corpus_test -- --nocapture

The held-out batch is measured by its own test, which asserts nothing about detection quality. Re-running it prints the same numbers; the committed report is only rewritten when the variable is supplied, which is what keeps the first run from being silently replaced by a later, tuned one:

HELDOUT_V2_REPORT=corpus/heldout_v2_report.json cargo test \
    --test heldout_v2_measurement_test -- --nocapture

The regression test prints per-category recall, every miss, every false positive, and every category-attribution mismatch, then fails if any list is non-empty or if recall/FPR cross the regression thresholds.

docs.title: What is not measured
docs.text:
• No independent or third-party evaluation. Every batch, including the held-out one, is hand-written in this repository by the same author as the engine. heldout_v10 was a real out-of-sample estimate of those payloads; its one-shot recall / 0.0% FPR is frozen in heldout_v10_report.json, while the current engine measures 100%/0.0% on the same batch and the in-sample 100%/0% rows above are not. Neither number says anything about traffic that was not imagined: no customer access log has ever been measured against this engine.
  • No comparison against real WAF products. The Python harness (run_benchmark.py) runs local stand-ins written for this repository. Rows named Coraza, SafeLine, ModSecurity or "probabilistic NLP" are reimplementations, not those products. They must never be cited as vendor benchmarks.
  • No production soak. No staged rollout, no traffic replay at scale, no long-running memory or rule-update testing.
  • No TLS or WebSocket handling in the standalone proxy. TLS terminates in front of it; WebSocket upgrades are rejected.
  • Prebuilt artifacts under dist/ and releases/ are stale. They were built before the claims were corrected and still contain the old banner text. Rebuild or delete them before publishing; do not ship them as current.

docs.title: How to reproduce
docs.text:
Two different numbers get quoted in these documents and they come from two different corpora. Do not expect one command to print the other one:

what you run corpus benign controls what it prints status of that corpus cargo run --release -- benchmark -r 10000 corpus/independent_v1.json 16 100% recall, 0.0% FPR in-sample regression floor: every miss in it was used to fix the engine ../target/release/satbench.exe --corpus benchmarks/real_comparative/corpus/heldout_v10.jsonl heldout_v10.jsonl (70 attacks, 44 benign) 44 one-shot: frozen result, 0.0% FPR (corpus/heldout_v10_report.json); current engine: 100%/0.0% post-tuning diagnostic (corpus/heldout_v10_post_tuning_report.json) current behaviour is the post-tuning diagnostic; the frozen one-shot estimate stays in heldout_v10_report.json cargo run --release --bin satbench -- --corpus benchmarks/real_comparative/corpus/unified_v1.jsonl unified_v1.jsonl floors — 100% recall, 0.0% FPR on in-sample splits regression floor, not an estimate

So the 0.0% false-positive rate on 44 controls above is the held-out measurement. tests/comparative_corpus_test.rs::heldout_v10_reproduction_matches_the_published_report re-derives it in-process. Batch v10 has since been spent by the protocol/DSL detector iteration: the engine now clears all 70 attacks, so the test asserts the one-shot figures remain intact as provenance and that live behaviour still matches corpus/heldout_v10_post_tuning_report.json — if the engine ever blocks a different set of v10 cases, the test fails. Per maintainer decision no heldout_v11 will be produced; the the frozen one-shot result one-shot remains the only publishable held-out estimate. tests/heldout_v2_measurement_test.rs is gated behind an environment variable and now documents a spent batch.

tests/comparative_corpus_test.rs calls the engine in-process — no HTTP, no proxy, no deployed host — and pins all three numbers as unit tests. Its held-out test asserts the reproduction, not the quality: if the engine ever blocks a different set of held-out cases, the test fails and says the batch is spent, which is the only way a held-out estimate can stay trustworthy.

# The frozen one-shot estimate lives in corpus/heldout_v10_report.json
# (frozen one-shot result). Re-running the corpus now prints the current
# engine behaviour (100%/0.0%) recorded in
# corpus/heldout_v10_post_tuning_report.json.
../target/release/satbench.exe --corpus benchmarks/real_comparative/corpus/heldout_v10.jsonl \
    --out benchmarks/real_comparative/results/satguardian/verdicts_heldout_v10_post_tuning.jsonl

# Detection regression (both in-sample corpora)
cargo test --test independent_corpus_test -- --nocapture

# The same measurements as in-process unit tests: no HTTP, no proxy, no deployed host
cargo test --test comparative_corpus_test -- --nocapture

# Full Rust suite
cargo test

# In-memory benchmark over the in-sample corpus
cargo run --release -- benchmark -r 10000

# Python reference harness (local stand-ins, in-sample)
python run_benchmark.py 1000

docs.title: Control boundary (what the paid tier actually does)
docs.text:
The product promise is: free, local protection; paid, ongoing review, update proposals and explanations — without giving up control of the WAF. As of 2026-11-04 the code matches that:

  • auto_sync_enabled defaults to false (src/config.rs), and the shipped waf_config.toml leaves it off. Cloud review runs only if you turn it on or invoke satguardian-waf sync-simplify / POST /api/waf/sync-simplify.
  • A review uploads recorded u128 feature vectors, not raw requests, and what comes back is stored in dynamic_clauses with applied = 0. Startup loads applied = 1 rows only.
  • A clause enters the engine after an explicit approval (satguardian-waf clauses apply <id>, or POST /api/waf/clauses/{id}/apply behind the admin token). reject deletes only unapplied proposals. Approved clauses are registered in an RwLock-guarded table capped at 4,096; there is no lock-free swap and no automatic apply anywhere in the client.
  • The Boolean minimizer (exactor-core-v128) is not a dependency of this crate and is not in any client artefact; minimization happens on the service side.
  • satguardian-advisor.py has no batch-approval option. Every proposal is decided one at a time by the operator running it.

tests/docs_claims_test.rs::cloud_review_stays_opt_in_and_never_applies_by_itself and tests/clause_approval_test.rs fail if any of that regresses.

docs.title: Why this file exists
docs.text:
Earlier versions of this repository published a benchmark that:

  • capped perfect accuracy at 99.9% and floored zero error rates at 0.1%;
  • labelled Python regex stand-ins as "Coraza WAF (OWASP CRS v4)" and "SafeLine WAF (Chaitin T1K)";
  • derived "3.38x faster", "15.0x faster" and "reduced false negatives by N percentage points" headlines from those stand-ins;
  • presented the numbers as production evidence.

Those claims were fabricated or misleading. The cap/floor logic is gone, the stand-ins are labelled, and the Rust benchmark now refuses to run without the versioned corpus. The guardrail tests in tests/docs_claims_test.rs fail the build if the banned claims or unlabelled comparisons return.

Treat a green test suite as "no known regressions on pinned inputs", not as "safe for production".

docs.title: Structured Grammar Inspection & Offline Rule Synthesis
docs.text:
Architectural Overview: In-Path Bitmask Evaluation plus Opt-In Cloud Rule Review Codebase Reference: src/engine/sat_solver.rs, src/cloud/satguardian_client.rs, src/ledger/sqlite_ledger.rs, src/api/server.rs, satguardian-advisor.py

Status: SATGuardian Edge WAF v0.3.0. Detection numbers in this document are in-sample results on a hand-written corpus plus one held-out run of the same author's payloads, and comparisons against local Python stand-ins. They are not vendor benchmarks and do not establish production readiness. There is no third-party evaluation. See STATUS.md.

docs.title: 1. Core Engineering Problem
docs.text:
Web application firewalls face an operational trade-off between latency, evasion resilience, and false positive rates:

  1. Unnormalized Signature WAFs: fast on simple strings but bypassable by inline comments, URL encoding or alternative DOM vectors. The local unnormalized-regex stand-in misses 47.0% of attacks on the in-repo stream; that is a property of the stand-in, not a measurement of ModSecurity.
  2. Multi-Target Anomaly Scoring WAFs (OWASP CRS / Coraza): broader coverage requires transformation passes and dozens of rule evaluations per request. The local CRS-style stand-in costs 0.2350 ms average in Python and misses 5.4% on the same stream. No claim is made about the real engine, whose rule count, paranoia level and tuning differ substantially.
  3. Probabilistic Token / NLP Classifiers: fixed token weights can fire on legitimate technical prose. The local hand-written heuristic scores a 24.6% false-positive rate on the in-repo benign controls; it is not a trained model.

docs.title: 2. The Two-Plane SATGuardian Architecture
docs.text:
SATGuardian resolves this trade-off by decoupling real-time edge inspection from out-of-band rule review, and by keeping the second plane behind an explicit operator decision:

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1. HOT PATH: SELF-HOSTED EDGE WAF                                          │
│    On your own node, no per-request fee, enforces with no network call     │
│                                                                            │
│ HTTP Request ──► Multi-Pass Lexer ──► 128-Bit FeatureVector (u128)         │
│    (src/ast/lexer.rs)        (src/ast/features.rs)                         │
│                  │                                                         │
│                  ▼                                                         │
│    Bitwise Rule Mask Evaluation (src/engine/sat_solver.rs)                 │
│    (minterm & required_mask) == expected_bits                              │
│    ~0.46 ms p50 in-memory, native Rust; TLS and proxy hops excluded (2026-11-10)          │
│           /                        \                                       │
│    [ALLOW: forward to upstream]   [BLOCK 403 + causal log]                 │
└────────────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
                                         │  Async SQLite ledger (waf_ledger.db)
                                         ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 2. CONTROL PLANE: OPT-IN CLOUD REVIEW → PROPOSALS → APPROVAL               │
│                                                                            │
│ waf_ledger.db ──► cloud review client ──► SATGuardian cloud synthesis      │
│   (ledger)      (satguardian_client.rs)   (satguardian.tech, off-repo)     │
│                                                                            │

docs.title: 2.1 Plane 1: In-Path Lexical & Bitmask Engine (src/engine/sat_solver.rs)
docs.text:
• Multi-Pass Canonicalization: Decodes nested URL encodings, strips inline comments (/**/), and extracts structural grammar tokens across five domains (ISLAND-SQLI, ISLAND-XSS, ISLAND-RCE, ISLAND-LFI, ISLAND-SSRF).
  • Bitwise Conjunction Evaluation: Evaluates compiled rules via u128 bitwise masks. Rules require structural conjunctions rather than isolated keywords. On the 16 benign controls in corpus/independent_v1.json the engine produced no false positives; that is an in-sample regression floor on a sample too small to generalize, and the one held-out batch measured a 7.0% false-positive rate on 57 controls.

docs.title: 2.2 Plane 2: Out-of-Band Cloud Review, Replay and Approval (src/cloud/satguardian_client.rs, src/ledger/sqlite_ledger.rs, satguardian-advisor.py)
docs.text:
• Minterm Harvesting: Requests that match no compiled cube are logged asynchronously to SQLite — without slowing down the hot path — as patterns awaiting analysis. They are candidates for review, not unprotected threats or gaps in coverage.
  • Opt-in Upload, Off by Default: Nothing is sent anywhere unless auto_sync_enabled is turned on (false by default in src/config.rs and waf_config.toml), the operator runs satguardian-waf sync-simplify, or a token-authenticated POST /api/waf/sync-simplify hits the local API.
  • Cloud Synthesis Is a Service, Not a Component of This Repository: The client posts its variable catalogue and minterms to https://satguardian.tech/api/simplify; the Boolean minimization over the {AND, OR, NOT, XOR} basis runs there. The minimizer is server-side, is not distributed to customers, and its internal algorithm and reduction cost are not characterized in this codebase. The client only compiles the returned equation into (required_mask, expected_bits) clauses (compile_equation_to_clauses()) and evaluates them.
  • Results Arrive as Proposals: Each compiled clause is written to dynamic_clauses with applied = 0. Proposals are never registered in the running engine and are skipped at startup, which loads approved clauses only (load_applied_clauses()).
  • Digital-Twin Replay (SimulationAgent): The advisor replays its own candidates against the benign requests recorded in waf_ledger.db and reports collisions, so the operator sees the evidence before deciding. Collision counts depend on the ledger contents and are not a fixed guarantee.
  • Approval Is the Only Thing That Enforces: satguardian-waf clauses apply <id> (from the next start) or POST /api/waf/clauses/{id}/apply on a running process registers one clause in the engine; reject deletes only a proposal and never removes a rule already in force.

docs.title: 4. Commercial & Operational Continuity Model
docs.text:
The model in one sentence: free, you get local protection on your own node; paying, you get continuous review of new patterns, update proposals and explanations — without ever giving up control of your WAF.

  1. Self-Hosted Traffic, by Default Offline: The Edge WAF runs entirely on your own infrastructure (standalone binary, reverse proxy in front of Nginx/Apache/IIS, or an Envoy sidecar in Kubernetes). There is no DNS CNAME redirection through external bastions, and with the default configuration the node makes no outbound call at all: auto_sync_enabled is false.
  2. Edge Inspection Carries No Per-Request Fee: In-path request inspection is free and unlimited; the engine's rule set is local, so it keeps enforcing with no network.
  3. Paid Cloud Review, Metered in Security Units (SU): A paid plan covers the SATGuardian cloud synthesis service — reviewing the patterns your node recorded and sending back update proposals with the equation and reduction they came from. SU accounting is based on the variables and minterms the service compresses. If the monthly SU quota is exhausted (HTTP 402 SU_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED), cloud review pauses while the local Edge WAF keeps enforcing the rules you already approved.
  4. Control Stays With the Operator: Cloud results are proposals stored in your own ledger. They enforce only after you approve them, one at a time, with satguardian-waf clauses apply <id> or the admin-token API. Rejecting a proposal cannot remove protection that is already in force, and turning the cloud off entirely leaves a fully functioning local WAF.

docs.title: SATGuardian Methodology: Lexical Tokenization, Bitmask Evaluation & Out-of-Band Cloud Rule Review
docs.text:
Technical Architecture Specification Codebase Reference: src/ast/lexer.rs, src/ast/features.rs, src/engine/sat_solver.rs, src/cloud/satguardian_client.rs, src/ledger/sqlite_ledger.rs, src/api/server.rs

Status: SATGuardian Edge WAF v0.3.0. Detection evidence is limited to a small in-sample corpus plus one held-out run of hand-written payloads, and there is no third-party evaluation; see STATUS.md.

docs.title: 1. Architectural Separation: Hot Path vs. Opt-In Control Plane
docs.text:
A core engineering principle of SATGuardian Edge WAF is the strict separation between in-path request evaluation (which must execute in microseconds with predictable latency) and out-of-band rule review (which is opt-in, runs against the SATGuardian cloud service, and ends in a proposal the operator approves).

Subsystem Execution Path Implemented Algorithm Computational Complexity Measured Latency Lexical Decoder & Tokenizer In-Path (Edge WAF) Iterative URL/HTML decoding + comment stripping + token scan (src/ast/lexer.rs) \(O(L)\) where \(L\) is payload byte length ~6–10 µs (Rust, in-memory) Bitmask Rule Evaluator In-Path (Edge WAF) 128-bit FeatureVector bitwise comparison (src/engine/sat_solver.rs) \(O(R)\) bitwise operations (\(R \le 64\) rules) ~4–6 µs (Rust, in-memory) Total Edge Hot Path In-Path (Edge WAF) Combined Lexer + Bitmask Evaluator Linear in payload size, constant per rule ~0.46 ms p50 / ~0.94 ms avg (in-memory, re-measured 2026-11-10) SATGuardian cloud synthesis Outside this repository (the service at satguardian.tech) Boolean minimization over the {AND, OR, NOT, XOR} basis Not characterized here; the client does not ship or run a minimizer Not measured in this repository Clause compiler (client side) Out-of-Band (src/cloud/satguardian_client.rs) compile_equation_to_clauses() parses the returned equation into (required_mask, expected_bits) pairs Linear in the number of literals Not measured in this repository Digital Twin Verifier Out-of-Band (satguardian-advisor.py) Historical replay over benign SQLite ledger (waf_ledger.db) \(O(N_{\text{benign}})\) ~50 ms for 1,663 benign logs in the bundled demo ledger

Important Clarification: SATGuardian does not execute an NP-complete backtracking SAT solver (such as DPLL or CDCL) on the live HTTP request path. The request path is a bitwise conjunction test over a fixed-width u128 feature vector. The algebraic minimization that turns recorded minterms into compact clauses is a property of the SATGuardian cloud synthesis service: it runs server-side, it is not distributed to customers, and this repository contains only the client that calls it, the code that compiles its answer into bitmasks, and the code that evaluates those bitmasks after an operator approves them.

docs.title: 2. Stage 1: Multi-Pass Lexical Normalization (src/ast/lexer.rs)
docs.text:
Attackers frequently evade traditional signature WAFs by nesting encodings (e.g., double or triple URL encoding ..%25252f, HTML entity encoding, or inline SQL comments /**/).

SATGuardian's lexer (AstLexer, with normalize_string for the decode passes and tokenize_request for the request path) applies a bounded, deterministic normalization pipeline before extracting grammatical tokens: 1. Iterative Percent-Decoding: Unwinds nested URL encodings up to a fixed recursion bound so obfuscated sequences resolve to their canonical ASCII characters. 2. Comment & Whitespace Canonicalization: Strips inline C/SQL comments (/* ... */) and collapses redundant whitespace so UNION/**/ALL/**/SELECT normalizes cleanly. 3. Contextual Token Extraction: Scans the normalized stream to identify structural tokens across five security domains ("Certainty Islands"): - ISLAND-SQLI: Quote delimiters, boolean tautologies ('1'='1', 1=1), UNION SELECT projections, stacked DDL (; DROP TABLE), and time-delay primitives (SLEEP, WAITFOR DELAY, BENCHMARK). - ISLAND-XSS: Executable <script> blocks, inline DOM event handlers (onerror=, onload=), <svg/onload>, and javascript:/data: pseudo-protocols. - ISLAND-RCE: Shell chaining operators (;, |, &&, `, $()) coupled with system binaries (cat, whoami, bash, curl, powershell) or dynamic evaluation sinks (os.system, eval(), subprocess). - ISLAND-LFI: Directory traversal sequences (../, ..\) and direct kernel/system file descriptors (/etc/passwd, /proc/self/environ, win.ini). - ISLAND-SSRF: Internal cloud metadata targets (169.254.169.254), loopback addresses (127.0.0.1, localhost), and non-HTTP proxy schemes (gopher://, dict://, file://).

docs.title: 3. Stage 2: 128-Bit Feature Vector & Bitmask Evaluation (src/ast/features.rs, src/engine/sat_solver.rs)
docs.text:
During inspection, extracted lexical properties and HTTP metadata are packed into a 128-bit integer (FeatureVector { bits: u128 }; the current catalogue names 40 of those bits):

// src/engine/sat_solver.rs — conjunction test for an approved compiled clause
let dyn_rules = self.dynamic_clauses.read().unwrap();
for clause in dyn_rules.iter() {
    if (fv.bits & clause.required_mask) == clause.expected_bits {
        // the request violates this clause: record the rule id, the active token
        // set and the boolean formula in the causal proof trace
    }
}

docs.title: Why SATGuardian Uses Bitmask Conjunctions
docs.text:
1. Structural Context vs. Substring Matching: A benign user comment containing the words "script" and "character" activates isolated keyword flags, which causes the local token-weight stand-in to produce false positives (24.6% on the in-repo stream). In SATGuardian, rule SAT-XSS-01 requires the simultaneous presence of TAG_OPEN \(\land\) SCRIPT_ELEMENT \(\land\) DOM_EXEC; the pinned corpus records no benign collision for it, which is an in-sample regression observation. The current held-out batch (benchmarks/real_comparative/corpus/heldout_v10.jsonl) was run once on 2026-11-08 before any fix: the frozen one-shot estimate is frozen one-shot result on 70 attacks and 0.0% false-positive rate on 44 controls (95% CI 0.0–8.0%), and the current engine measures 100%/0.0% on the same batch as a post-tuning diagnostic. The earlier heldout_v2 figure (56.1%/7.0%) remains for provenance, and no third-party evaluation exists.
  2. Predictable CPU Execution: Bitwise operations on a u128 register execute in a few CPU clock cycles without backtracking, which is why the hot path has no ReDoS-style blow-up on the corpus payloads.
  3. Human-Auditable Causal Traces: Every blocked request records the exact rule ID, active token set, and boolean clause in waf_ledger.db (e.g., (SELECT_PROJECTION AND UNION_CLAUSE) violates [SAT-SQLI-02] -> ACTION_BLOCK [sql_injection]).

docs.title: 4. Stage 3: Out-of-Band Cloud Review, Replay and Approval (src/cloud/satguardian_client.rs, src/ledger/sqlite_ledger.rs, satguardian-advisor.py, src/api/server.rs)
docs.text:
When the Edge WAF encounters anomalous high-entropy requests or repeated hostile bursts that do not match an existing compiled cube, it logs the observed 128-bit minterm in the novel_anomalies table of waf_ledger.db. Those rows are patterns awaiting analysis: they say the engine did not recognize the shape, not that the shape got through.

Review is opt-in. auto_sync_enabled defaults to false in src/config.rs and in waf_config.toml, so with the shipped configuration no minterm ever leaves the node. When an operator enables it, runs satguardian-waf sync-simplify, or calls the token-authenticated POST /api/waf/sync-simplify, the client bundles the variable catalogue plus the pending minterms and POSTs them to the SATGuardian cloud synthesis service at https://satguardian.tech/api/simplify.

What happens next is deliberately split in two:

  1. Minimization on the service. The reduction of those minterms into a compact equation over the {AND, OR, NOT, XOR} basis is performed by the SATGuardian cloud synthesizer. It is server-side code: it is not in this repository, it is not distributed to customers, and its internal algorithm and clause-count behaviour are not characterized by anything in this codebase.
  2. Compilation on the client. SatguardianCloudClient::compile_equation_to_clauses (src/cloud/satguardian_client.rs) parses the returned equation into (required_mask, expected_bits) pairs — the same representation the built-in rules use, so evaluation stays a single AND plus a comparison. A response the client cannot parse is rejected with invalid_cloud_equation; nothing is loaded on a parse failure.
  3. Storage as proposals. Each compiled clause is written to dynamic_clauses with applied = 0 (SqliteLedger::propose_dynamic_clause). It does not enter the running engine, and startup ignores it: load_applied_clauses() selects applied = 1 only. The sync response states this — "status": "proposed", "Nothing was applied to the running rule set".
  4. Replay evidence for the operator. The advisor (satguardian-advisor.py) replays candidate bitmasks against the benign requests recorded in waf_ledger.db and reports collisions per run, so the person deciding can see what the candidate would have blocked. The gate is only as good as the recorded benign traffic; it does not establish a fixed false-positive rate.
  5. Approval, the only step that changes enforcement. satguardian-waf clauses apply <id> marks a proposal approved (it registers when the proxy starts); POST /api/waf/clauses/{id}/apply additionally calls engine.register_dynamic_clause() on the live process, so new requests see it without restarting the proxy or dropping connections. clauses reject <id> / DELETE /api/waf/clauses/{id} deletes only a proposal — a rule already enforcing is never removed by it. All of these sit behind the existing admin token.

The practical consequence is the product promise: the node protects itself for free and offline; the paid service contributes continuous review of new patterns, proposals and explanations; and the operator stays in control of what the WAF actually enforces.

docs.title: SATGuardian Edge WAF — System Architecture & Implementation Reference
docs.text:
Repository: satguardian Version: v0.3.0 Scope: Implementation architecture (Rust hot path & Python control plane)

Status: SATGuardian Edge WAF v0.3.0. Metrics in this document are in-sample measurements on a hand-written corpus, plus one held-out run on the same author's payloads. The Python comparison harness runs local stand-ins, not real vendor products, and no third-party evaluation exists. See STATUS.md and corpus/README.md.

docs.title: 1. Architectural Overview
docs.text:
satguardian is a hybrid Web Application Firewall (WAF) divided into two strictly decoupled execution planes:

  1. In-Path Edge Data Plane (Native Rust — src/): Evaluates HTTP requests in memory (hundreds of microseconds per payload; no network hop included) using multi-pass lexical normalization, a 128-bit feature bitmask (FeatureVector { bits: u128 }, 40 named variables in the current catalogue), and bitwise rule comparisons ((minterm & required_mask) == expected_bits). This plane is self-contained: it enforces the rules already in the process and needs no network access to do so.
  2. Out-of-Band Control & Cloud Review Plane (Rust & Python — src/cloud/satguardian_client.rs, src/ledger/sqlite_ledger.rs, satguardian-advisor.py): Reads the SQLite forensic audit ledger (waf_ledger.db) and, only when the operator turns cloud review on (auto_sync_enabled, false by default in src/config.rs and waf_config.toml), sends collected u128 anomaly minterms to the SATGuardian cloud synthesis service at satguardian.tech. Boolean minimization runs on that service, not in this repository: the client receives a reduced equation, compiles it into bitmask clauses, and stores them as proposals (dynamic_clauses.applied = 0). Proposals do not enter the running engine and are not loaded at startup. A separate explicit action — satguardian-waf clauses apply <id> or POST /api/waf/clauses/{id}/apply — registers one clause in the engine.

docs.title: 3. Cloud Review and the Operator Approval Gate
docs.text:
The edge node is the default; the cloud is an opt-in review service. Free, you get local protection on your own node. Paying, you get continuous review of new patterns, update proposals and explanations — without ever giving up control of your WAF.

  1. Nothing leaves the node unless you say so. auto_sync_enabled defaults to false in src/config.rs and in waf_config.toml. With the default configuration the process never uploads observed anomalies.
  2. Three entry points, one behaviour. The opt-in timer worker (every autonomous_sync_interval_secs, default 300 s), the CLI satguardian-waf sync-simplify and POST /api/waf/sync-simplify all send the pending minterms of novel_anomalies to the cloud and store what comes back as proposals: rows in dynamic_clauses with applied = 0.
  3. Proposals do not enforce. A proposal is not registered in the running engine and is not loaded at startup — main.rs calls ledger.load_applied_clauses(), which selects applied = 1 only. The sync response says so explicitly ("status": "proposed", "Nothing was applied to the running rule set").
  4. Approval is a separate, explicit action, always behind the existing admin token (require_admin_token in src/api/server.rs):
Decision CLI HTTP API List open proposals satguardian-waf clauses list GET /api/waf/clauses/pending Approve one satguardian-waf clauses apply <id> POST /api/waf/clauses/{id}/apply Discard one satguardian-waf clauses reject <id> DELETE /api/waf/clauses/{id}

clauses apply marks the row approved, so the clause enforces from the next start; approving through the HTTP API on a running process additionally calls engine.register_dynamic_clause(), and the response reports enforcing_now. Registering on the shared in-memory rule set is what makes an approved clause take effect for subsequent requests without restarting the proxy or dropping connections. 5. Rejecting cannot weaken you. reject_dynamic_clause deletes a row where applied = 0. A rule already enforcing is never removed by it. 6. pending_anomalies are patterns awaiting analysis. They are logged minterms the engine did not recognize, not unprotected threats and not a coverage gap.

docs.title: Comparative Architecture Notes: SATGuardian and Local Stand-Ins
docs.text:
Subject: how SATGuardian differs from signature, anomaly-scoring, semantic and probabilistic WAF designs, and what the repository actually measures Target system: satguardian v0.3.0

Status: SATGuardian Edge WAF v0.3.0. The Python harness runs local reimplementations of each technique, not Coraza, SafeLine, ModSecurity or a trained NLP model. Detection numbers below are in-sample regression floors on a hand-written corpus, except the single held-out run called out separately. The only real-product measurement is the 2026-11-09 head-to-head against Aegis Community Edition v1.1.0 in §2.5; there is still no third-party evaluation. See STATUS.md and corpus/README.md.

docs.title: 1. What is being compared
docs.text:
1. SATGuardian: multi-pass lexical normalization (src/ast/lexer.rs), a 128-bit feature bitmask (FeatureVector), and bitwise rule evaluation in src/engine/sat_solver.rs. Rule review is a separate, opt-in step: the client can send recorded minterms to the SATGuardian cloud synthesis service (satguardian.tech), which minimizes them server-side and returns compiled clauses. The minimizer is not part of this repository and is not distributed to customers; the client stores what comes back as proposals that an operator must approve before anything enforces.
  2. CRS-style stand-in (not Coraza): a few hand-written regex rules with a simple anomaly score over decoded request targets. It does not model the real CRS rule count, paranoia levels or exclusions.
  3. Semantic-token stand-in (not SafeLine): single-pass decode plus a small pattern list. It is not Chaitin's engine.
  4. Probabilistic token stand-in (not a trained model): fixed keyword weights and Shannon entropy. It is not a trained classifier.
  5. Unnormalized regex stand-in (not ModSecurity): deliberately naive signatures over raw fields.

The point of the harness is to regression-test the Python reference port and to illustrate design trade-offs. It cannot rank real products.

docs.title: 2. What the harness measures
docs.text:
python run_benchmark.py 1000 samples the in-repo payload list (1,000 requests, 50% attacks by default). Only the SATGuardian row is this project's code.

docs.title: 2.2 The one held-out measurement
docs.text:
The 100%/0% rows above describe cases that were used to drive the fixes. The current out-of-sample number in this repository comes from benchmarks/real_comparative/corpus/heldout_v10.jsonl (70 attacks, 44 benign controls), measured once on 2026-11-08 before any fix:

Metric Held-out result Recall on 70 attacks frozen one-shot (27/70); current engine 100% (70/70) post-tuning diagnostic False-positive rate on 44 controls 0.0% (0/44), 95% CI 0.0–8.0%

The earlier corpus/heldout_v2.json measurement (56.1% recall / 7.0% FPR on 98 attacks and 57 controls, one run on 2026-11-04) remains published for provenance; batches v3–v9 were each measured once and spent as tuning inputs. The batches are hand-written from public payload catalogues and their benign controls are imagined traffic, not a customer access log, so this measures those payloads and nothing wider. No third-party evaluation exists, and corpus/README.md records that tuning against a batch would invalidate it. The OWASP CRS v4.30 suite is measured in-sample at 82.0% recall — a coverage check against the rule set's own tests, not an independent benchmark.

docs.title: 2.5 The first real-product head-to-head (Aegis Community v1.1.0)
docs.text:
On 2026-11-09 SATGuardian was replayed against Aegis Community Edition v1.1.0 — a shipping WAF built on the Coraza engine with the bundled OWASP CRS 4.25.1 LTS ruleset at paranoia level 1, blocking mode — over real HTTP on localhost, on the same corpus files. This is the first measurement in this repository against an actual product; earlier competitor rows remain local stand-ins. Artifacts: benchmarks/real_comparative/results/aegis/ (RUN.json, aegis_v10.jsonl, aegis_crs.jsonl).

Corpus SATGuardian Aegis + CRS 4.25.1 PL1 crs_v430.jsonl attacks 82.0% (3,321/4,050) 80.7% (3,268/4,050) heldout_v10.jsonl attacks 100% post-tuning diagnostic; frozen one-shot 68.6% (48/70) heldout_v10.jsonl controls 0.0% FPR post-tuning diagnostic; frozen one-shot 0.0% 36.4% (16/44) benign_heldout_v3_v10.jsonl (665 pooled benign controls) 0.5% (3/665; v10-only non-spent subset 0/44) 22.9% (152/665)

Union of both engines on crs_v430: 92.9% recall; intersection: 69.8%. The engines miss different rule families — e.g. SATGuardian detects 44/44 vs Aegis 7/44 on CRS rule 934140, while Aegis detects 210/330 vs SATGuardian 162/330 on rule 944300 — so a cascade is the natural deployment shape.

Limits: Aegis ran CRS 4.25.1 (the corpus targets 4.30), paranoia level 1, community edition, plain HTTP, localhost, dummy upstream, default rate limiter disabled. Latency is not comparable across the two rows (full HTTP round-trip vs in-process evaluation). One run, one configuration — not a product ranking.

The false-positive gap is the sharpest measured difference: pooled over all 665 benign controls from batches v3–v10, Aegis blocked 152 (22.9% FPR, 95% CI 19.8–26.2%) while SATGuardian blocked 3 (0.5%, CI 0.2–1.3%). For SATGuardian only the 44 v10 controls are non-spent (v3–v9 benign controls were tuning inputs); for Aegis every control was fresh. The controls are imagined traffic authored inside this project, not a customer access log, so the absolute rates describe these payloads — but the ~45× gap between engines on identical inputs is the measured fact.

docs.title: 3.1 Anomaly scoring
docs.text: Anomaly scoring transforms several request targets and evaluates many rules. That buys coverage and configurability at a per-request CPU cost. The local stand-in implements only a small approximation (20 regex rules), so its latency is not a measurement of real CRS cost. SATGuardian instead normalizes once and evaluates bitmasks; whether that trade-off holds against a real deployment is untested.

docs.title: 3.2 Semantic tokenization
docs.text: Single-pass decoding plus token patterns is cheap, but it can miss nested encodings. The stand-in misses 11.2% of the in-repo attacks, largely on double-encoded traversal. SATGuardian decodes multiple layers; on the pinned corpus it catches those cases after the 2026-11-01 fixes. The corpus was used to drive those fixes, so this is not held-out evidence.

docs.title: 3.3 Probabilistic token scoring
docs.text: Fixed token weights misfire on benign technical prose. The local heuristic blocks 24.6% of the benign controls in the in-repo stream. SATGuardian requires structural conjunctions, and produced no false positives on the 16 benign corpus controls — an in-sample regression floor on sixteen cases. The single held-out batch is the relevant comparison: it measured a 7.0% false-positive rate on 57 controls (95% CI 2.8–16.7%), which is what the design actually costs on payloads that were not used for tuning.

docs.title: 3.4 Unnormalized regex
docs.text: Raw signature scanning is the cheapest row in the harness and the leakiest on obfuscated payloads (47.0% FNR in this stream). This illustrates why normalization matters; it does not measure ModSecurity.

docs.title: 4. Demonstration Ledger (waf_ledger.db)
docs.text:
The bundled SQLite ledger is demo data used to exercise the advisor pipeline: 3,799 transactions (2,136 blocked, 1,663 allowed). Advisor candidates are replayed against the benign rows and collision counts are printed per run. The ledger is not independent evidence of detection quality and is not a customer tenant. Minterms the engine did not recognize sit in novel_anomalies as patterns awaiting analysis — they are review candidates, not unprotected threats — and cloud review is off unless auto_sync_enabled is turned on. Whatever the service returns is stored as a proposal (dynamic_clauses.applied = 0) and only enforces after satguardian-waf clauses apply <id>. Regenerate the audit with:

python satguardian-advisor.py --report-md audit_report.md

1. Forensic ledger walkthrough: the bundled waf_ledger.db contains recorded demo traffic that can be re-analysed with satguardian-advisor.py. Row counts depend on the ledger revision; regenerate the audit before quoting them.

docs.text:
1. Latency is in-memory only. The Rust engine evaluates rules in tens of microseconds per payload on this machine. No end-to-end proxy latency has been characterized.
  2. The 100%/0% corpus rows are regression floors. They pass because those cases were used to drive fixes. docs.title: Kubernetes & Envoy Proxy Integration Guide (Native Sidecar Pattern, Lab Configuration)
docs.text:
Deployment Architecture: self-hosted edge inspection (lab configuration) Codebase Reference: src/envoy/ext_authz.rs, envoy/envoy-uds.yaml, envoy/kubernetes-sidecar.yaml

Status: SATGuardian Edge WAF v0.3.0. This integration has been exercised in a lab on our own machine. It has not been run under real traffic, and nothing here is production evidence. See STATUS.md.

docs.title: 1. Overview: Sidecar Authorization in a Lab Pod
docs.text:
For Kubernetes workloads and service meshes (Istio / Envoy), SATGuardian Edge WAF can run as a small self-contained Rust sidecar container next to the Envoy proxy in the same pod.

Envoy delegates incoming HTTP request authorization to the local SATGuardian daemon via the ext_authz filter over an in-memory Unix Domain Socket (/var/run/satguardian/waf.sock) or a loopback HTTP socket, avoiding a network hop.

                      ┌─────────────────────────── Kubernetes Pod ───────────────────────────┐
                      │                                                                      │
Incoming Traffic ────►│  [ Envoy Proxy ] ──(ext_authz UDS)──► [ SATGuardian Rust Sidecar ]   │
  (Ingress/Mesh)      │         │                               (~0.46 ms p50 in-memory eval, 2026-11-10)  │
                      │         │ (HTTP 200 OK / Allow)                     │                │
                      │         ▼                                           ▼                │
                      │  [ Upstream App Container ]              [ Local waf_ledger.db ]     │
                      └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Why the Sidecar Shape Is Interesting
docs.text:
1. Microsecond-scale engine evaluation (in memory only): satguardian-waf benchmark -r 10000 measures in-memory lexical and bitmask evaluation at roughly 0.46 ms p50 and 0.94 ms mean, with p99 around 6 ms depending on load (re-measured 2026-11-10). These numbers exclude the UDS hop, Envoy itself and the upstream service; end-to-end sidecar latency has not been characterized.
  2. Traffic stays inside your cluster, and the edge costs nothing per request: all HTTP payloads are inspected locally, with no external DNS CNAME routing and no per-request fee. With the shipped defaults (auto_sync_enabled = false in waf_config.toml) the sidecar makes no outbound call at all.
  3. Rule updates are an operator decision, not a sync side effect: cloud review returns clauses that are stored in the ledger as proposals (dynamic_clauses.applied = 0); the sync never touches the running engine. Approval is a separate action — satguardian-waf clauses apply <id> against the ledger, or an admin-token POST /api/waf/clauses/{id}/apply on the management API, which additionally registers the clause in the live process so subsequent requests see it without restarting the pod or dropping connections.
  4. Continuity if the cloud is not there: if the monthly Security Units (SU) quota is exhausted (HTTP 402 SU_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED) or satguardian.tech is unreachable, no new proposals arrive. Every sidecar keeps inspecting and blocking with the rule set it already has, because enforcement is entirely local.

docs.title: 2. Envoy ext_authz Configuration (envoy/envoy-uds.yaml)
docs.text:
The daemon in src/envoy/ext_authz.rs serves the ext_authz HTTP service (it answers a plain HTTP check request with 200 or 403), so Envoy is configured with http_service, not grpc_service. The snippet below is the configuration shipped in this repository:

          - name: envoy.filters.http.ext_authz
            typed_config:
              "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.ext_authz.v3.ExtAuthz
              http_service:
                server_uri:
                  uri: "http://unix/ext_authz"
                  cluster: satguardian_waf_uds
                  timeout: 0.25s
                authorization_request:
                  allowed_headers:
                    patterns:
                    - exact: "authorization"
                    - exact: "cookie"
                    - exact: "x-forwarded-for"
                    - exact: "user-agent"
                    - exact: "content-type"
                    - prefix: "x-"
              with_request_body:
                max_request_bytes: 65536
                pack_as_bytes: false
                allow_partial_message: true

clusters:
  - name: satguardian_waf_uds
    connect_timeout: 0.25s
    load_assignment:
      cluster_name: satguardian_waf_uds
      endpoints:
        - lb_endpoints:
            - endpoint:
                address:
                  pipe:
                    path: /var/run/satguardian/waf.sock

The sidecar terminates nothing: TLS is expected to end at Envoy. src/envoy/ext_authz.rs reads the original method and path from x-envoy-original-method / x-envoy-original-path when Envoy forwards them, and only trusts X-Forwarded-For from proxies listed in trusted_proxies.

docs.title: 3. Kubernetes Sidecar Manifest (envoy/kubernetes-sidecar.yaml)
docs.text:
The committed manifest mounts an emptyDir with medium: Memory so Envoy and the sidecar share one Unix Domain Socket, and starts the daemon in ext_authz mode:

      volumes:
        - name: satguardian-ipc
          emptyDir:
            medium: Memory
            sizeLimit: 64Mi
        - name: satguardian-ledger
          emptyDir: {}

      containers:
        - name: envoy-proxy
          image: envoyproxy/envoy:v1.30-latest
          args: ["-c", "/etc/envoy/envoy.yaml"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: envoy-config-vol
              mountPath: /etc/envoy
            - name: satguardian-ipc
              mountPath: /var/run/satguardian

        - name: satguardian-waf-sidecar
          image: satguardian/satguardian-waf:v0.3.0
          command: ["/usr/local/bin/satguardian-waf"]
          args:
            - "envoy-authz"
            - "--socket"
            - "/var/run/satguardian/waf.sock"
          env:
            - name: WAF_MODE
              value: "block"
            - name: SATGUARDIAN_API_URL
              value: "https://satguardian.tech/api/simplify"
            - name: SATGUARDIAN_API_KEY            # optional; only needed for cloud review
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: satguardian-cloud-credentials
                  key: api-token
                  optional: true
            - name: WAF_DATABASE_PATH
              value: "/var/lib/satguardian/waf_ledger.db"
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "100m"
              memory: "128Mi"
            limits:
              cpu: "1"
              memory: "512Mi"
          volumeMounts:
            - name: satguardian-ipc
              mountPath: /var/run/satguardian
            - name: satguardian-ledger
              mountPath: /var/lib/satguardian

Two operational notes, both read straight off src/main.rs:

  • The ledger volume is emptyDir in the shipped manifest, so recorded traffic, patterns awaiting analysis and open proposals disappear with the pod. Persist /var/lib/satguardian on a real volume before treating the ledger as an audit record.
  • envoy-authz is a pure verifier. It mounts only the ext_authz router: no management API, and it starts from the compiled-in rule matrix rather than calling load_applied_clauses(), so a proposal you approve against that ledger does not silently become policy in the sidecar. If you want approved dynamic clauses and the approval API in one process, run the proxy command with envoy_ext_authz_addr (TCP, e.g. loopback) and admin_listen_addr set: run_server loads approved clauses (applied = 1) at startup and serves POST /api/waf/clauses/{id}/apply for live registration. The Unix Domain Socket path (--socket) exists only in envoy-authz today. Treat that split as a known limitation of the lab wiring, not as a hot-reload feature.

docs.title: ⚙️ SATGuardian Edge WAF — Configuration Reference
docs.text:
Status: SATGuardian Edge WAF v0.3.0. Detection has one held-out estimate (benchmarks/real_comparative/corpus/heldout_v10.jsonl, frozen one-shot result on 70 attacks, and 0.0% false positives on 44 controls, 95% CI 0.0–8.0%, run once 2026-11-08, same-author payloads, no third-party evaluation) — the current engine measures 100%/0.0% on the same batch as a post-tuning diagnostic; the earlier heldout_v2 figure (56.1%/7.0%) remains for provenance. The in-sample 100% / 0% rows in corpus/independent_v1.json are regression floors, not generalization estimates. See Project Status and the Detection Corpus.

This guide provides a field-by-field reference for configuring SATGuardian Edge WAF via waf_config.toml and environment variables.

The control rule in one line: free, you get local protection on your own node; paying, you get continuous review of new patterns, update proposals and explanations — without ever giving up control of your WAF. Every cloud result below is a proposal until you approve it.

docs.title: 📋 Configuration File Location
docs.text:
By default, SATGuardian looks for waf_config.toml in the current working directory. You can specify a custom configuration file path using the --config flag or the SATGUARDIAN_CONFIG environment variable:

# Using CLI flag
./satguardian-waf proxy --config /etc/satguardian/waf_config.toml

# Using environment variable
export SATGUARDIAN_CONFIG="/etc/satguardian/waf_config.toml"
./satguardian-waf proxy

docs.title: 🌐 1. Network & Core Defense Settings
docs.text:
Configures the inbound proxy listener, the target upstream application backend, and the active defense mode.

# Inbound HTTP listener address where SATGuardian intercepts incoming web traffic
listen_addr = "0.0.0.0:8080"

# Target upstream backend application (Nginx, Node.js, Python, Go, Java, PHP, IIS, etc.)
upstream_url = "http://127.0.0.1:3000"

# Defense mode:
#   "block"   - Detected requests are rejected with HTTP 403 Forbidden.
#   "monitor" - Dry-run mode: violations are logged to the ledger, traffic passes upstream.
mode = "block"

upstream_url must start with http:// or https:// — the client refuses to start otherwise. The listener itself is plain HTTP: this build does not terminate TLS and does not proxy WebSocket upgrades, so TLS belongs to an nginx/Envoy hop in front of it.

docs.title: 🥷 2. Anti-Reconnaissance Protection (Stealth Mode)
docs.text:
Prevents attackers from identifying your security stack through diagnostic response signatures.

# Enable clean web-standard responses
# true  -> Returns a generic HTTP 403 Forbidden without leaking rules, proofs, or server signatures.
# false -> Returns diagnostic JSON containing the causal trace (useful for debugging).
stealth_mode = true

# (Optional) Custom HTML or plain text body returned for blocked requests when stealth_mode = true
stealth_block_body = "<html><head><title>403 Forbidden</title></head><body><center><h1>403 Forbidden</h1><p>Access Denied by Security Policy</p></center></body></html>"

Per launch you can override the file: satguardian-waf proxy --verbose emits the diagnostic JSON, satguardian-waf proxy --stealth forces the generic block response.

docs.title: 🎛️ 3. Management API & Request Limits
docs.text:
The management API is what you use to look at and approve cloud proposals. It never runs on the public data-plane port.

# Dedicated listener for /api/waf/*. Set to "off" to disable the management API entirely.
admin_listen_addr = "127.0.0.1:10001"

# Bearer token required by every management route. Prefer the SATGUARDIAN_ADMIN_TOKEN
# environment variable over storing it in the file.
# admin_token = "change-me"

# Maximum accepted inbound request body (2 MiB).
max_body_bytes = 2097152

# Exact IPs or CIDR ranges of upstream proxies allowed to supply X-Forwarded-For /
# X-Real-IP / CF-Connecting-IP / True-Client-IP. Loopback is always trusted.
trusted_proxies = []
Route Purpose GET /health, GET /livez Liveness; the only routes that are not token-protected. POST /api/waf/inspect Evaluate one request payload and print the causal trace. GET /api/waf/metrics, /api/waf/rules, /api/waf/islands Read engine state. GET/POST /api/waf/islands/config Read or change the islands switches. GET/POST /api/waf/rules/customer, DELETE /api/waf/rules/customer/{id} Manage declarative business rules. POST /api/waf/sync-simplify One opt-in cloud review batch; the result is stored as proposals. GET /api/waf/clauses/pending List proposals waiting for a decision. POST /api/waf/clauses/{id}/apply The approval step — register the clause in the running engine. DELETE /api/waf/clauses/{id} Discard a proposal. Never removes a clause already enforcing.

With no admin token configured these routes answer 503 management_api_disabled. The listener is plain HTTP on loopback by default — if you expose it anywhere, put a TLS-terminating authenticated proxy in front.

docs.title: ☁️ 4. Cloud Review (Security Units - SU) & SQLite Ledger
docs.text:
Optional contact with satguardian.tech for Boolean rule synthesis, plus local forensic audit logging.

Boolean minimization is server-side only. This client normalizes a request into a 128-bit FeatureVector (u128), evaluates compiled clauses locally, and — only when you opt in — sends recorded minterms to the cloud endpoint and stores what comes back as proposals. No minimizer ships in the client binary or lives in this repository.

# SATGuardian cloud endpoint for Boolean rule synthesis
satguardian_api_url = "https://satguardian.tech/api/simplify"

# Cloud API Key (or configure via SATGUARDIAN_API_KEY environment variable)
satguardian_api_key = "ek_live_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"

# SQLite WAL Ledger database path: audit log, anomaly clustering and update proposals
database_path = "waf_ledger.db"

# Seconds between background cloud review runs. Only used when auto_sync_enabled is on.
autonomous_sync_interval_secs = 300

# Opt-in switch. False by default: nothing leaves the node unless you turn this on.
auto_sync_enabled = false

What auto_sync_enabled = true does and does not do. It only uploads the u128 feature vectors recorded as novel anomalies (patterns awaiting analysis) on that timer — not raw traffic, headers, bodies or client IPs. Results are stored with dynamic_clauses.applied = 0: they do not enter the running engine and are not loaded at startup. Making one enforce is a separate action you take:

./satguardian-waf clauses list
./satguardian-waf clauses apply <id>
./satguardian-waf clauses reject <id>

Review on demand instead of on a timer with ./satguardian-waf sync-simplify --limit 100 or POST /api/waf/sync-simplify.

Quota behavior: cloud synthesis is metered in Security Units (SU) per job and the balance is readable with satguardian-waf entitlement. A failed review call — including one rejected for an exhausted SU balance — is logged and simply produces no proposals; the Edge WAF keeps enforcing the last rule matrix you approved. The client treats every non-2xx answer as a generic cloud error today; there is no dedicated 402 SU_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED branch in this build. Local inspection is never metered.

docs.title: 🛡️ 5. Layer-7 Behavioral Defense & Rate Limiting
docs.text:
Protects against credential stuffing, brute force login floods, and Layer-7 HTTP floods using sliding window ring buffers.

# Enable stateful temporal ring buffer analysis
stateful_enabled = true

# Maximum total requests permitted per client IP across all endpoints within the sliding window
stateful_global_limit = 300

# Maximum permitted requests per client IP on sensitive authentication routes (/login, /auth, etc.)
stateful_auth_limit = 20

# Temporal sliding window duration in seconds (60s ring buffer)
stateful_window_secs = 60

# Isolation / jail quarantine duration in seconds for offending IPs (180s = 3 minutes)
stateful_ban_secs = 180

# (Optional) Redis URL for distributed multi-node cluster rate limiting
# redis_url = "redis://127.0.0.1:6379"

docs.title: 🔗 6. Envoy Proxy Native Integration (ext_authz)
docs.text:
Runs SATGuardian as an external authorization service for the envoy.filters.http.ext_authz filter.

# Inbound HTTP listener for Envoy's envoy.filters.http.ext_authz filter
envoy_ext_authz_addr = "0.0.0.0:9002"

This is the HTTP form of ext_authz: the service reads x-envoy-original-method and x-envoy-original-path and answers the check itself. The gRPC ext_authz protocol is not implemented in this build, and a Unix socket alternative is available via satguardian-waf envoy-authz --socket /var/run/waf.sock.

The check itself costs hundreds of microseconds in memory; the end-to-end latency your clients see still includes TLS, Envoy and your upstream, which this project does not measure.

docs.title: 🏝️ 7. Modular Certainty Islands ([islands])
docs.text:
Enable or disable pre-compiled domain-specific exploit shields.

[islands]
# WordPress Reconnaissance & Exploit Shield:
# Drops scanner probes targeting /wp-admin, /wp-login.php, xmlrpc.php, and plugin exploits.
# Set to false ONLY if your application legitimately runs WordPress.
wordpress_shield = true

# Sensitive Files & Backdoors Shield:
# Blocks discovery probes targeting /.env, /.git, phpMyAdmin, Spring actuator, and database dumps.
exposure_shield = true

# Modern Framework Exploits Shield:
# Blocks Log4j/JNDI injection, Spring Cloud SpEL, Laravel Ignition, and ThinkPHP RCE probes.
framework_shield = true

docs.title: 🎯 8. Customer Business Access Rules ([business_rules])
docs.text:
Declarative access control policies for specific route prefixes, HTTP methods, IP whitelists, blacklists, and mandatory headers.

[business_rules]
enabled = true

# Example 1: Enforce Strict HTTP Method Whitelist on API endpoints
[[business_rules.rules]]
id = "biz-api-methods"
name = "Strict API Method Whitelist"
path_prefix = "/api/v1/"
allowed_methods = ["GET", "POST", "PUT", "DELETE", "OPTIONS"]
blocked_methods = ["TRACE", "CONNECT", "PATCH"]
allowed_ips = []
blocked_ips = []
required_headers = []
max_body_bytes = 10485760 # 10 MB payload ceiling
enabled = true

# Example 2: IP-Restricted Internal Administrative Gateway
[[business_rules.rules]]
id = "biz-admin-gateway"
name = "Admin Portal IP Restricted Access"
path_prefix = "/internal/admin/"
allowed_methods = ["GET", "POST"]
blocked_methods = []
allowed_ips = ["127.0.0.1", "10.0.0.1", "192.168.1.100"] # Authorized admin IPs
blocked_ips = []
required_headers = ["X-Admin-Token"] # Mandatory administrative header
max_body_bytes = 1048576 # 1 MB body ceiling
enabled = true

docs.title: Parameter Reference for Business Rules:
docs.text:
Parameter Type Description id String Unique rule identifier. name String Human-readable description of the rule. path_prefix String URL path prefix target (e.g. /api/, /admin/). allowed_methods Array Allowed HTTP methods (e.g. ["GET", "POST"]). blocked_methods Array Blocked HTTP methods (e.g. ["TRACE", "PATCH"]). allowed_ips Array Client IP whitelist (if non-empty, unlisted IPs are blocked). blocked_ips Array Client IP blacklist (listed IPs are dropped). required_headers Array Mandatory HTTP headers required for request approval. max_body_bytes Integer Maximum permitted HTTP body size in bytes. enabled Boolean true to activate rule, false to disable.

These rules are yours and live in your file. They are separate from cloud proposals: a proposal you approve is stored in the ledger as a dynamic clause, not written into [business_rules].

docs.title: 🔑 9. Environment Variables Reference
docs.text:
Variable Description Example SATGUARDIAN_CONFIG Overrides path to configuration file export SATGUARDIAN_CONFIG="/etc/waf_config.toml" SATGUARDIAN_API_KEY Overrides the cloud API key (SU metering) export SATGUARDIAN_API_KEY="ek_live_12345" SATGUARDIAN_ADMIN_TOKEN Bearer token for every management API route; without it the routes return 503 export SATGUARDIAN_ADMIN_TOKEN="$(openssl rand -hex 32)" RUST_LOG Configures logging verbosity export RUST_LOG="info" or export RUST_LOG="satguardian_waf=debug"

Most TOML fields also accept a WAF_* override (WAF_LISTEN_ADDR, WAF_UPSTREAM_URL, WAF_MODE, WAF_STEALTH_MODE, WAF_ADMIN_LISTEN_ADDR, WAF_MAX_BODY_BYTES, WAF_TRUSTED_PROXIES, WAF_DATABASE_PATH, ENVOY_EXT_AUTHZ_ADDR, SATGUARDIAN_API_URL), which wins over the file.

For the update loop (opt-in upload → proposals → your approval) and the CLI/Python tooling, see Operations & Tooling Guide.

docs.title: 📖 SATGuardian Edge WAF — Operations, Configuration & Tooling Manual
docs.text:
This guide documents how to configure and operate the SATGuardian Edge WAF client, and how to use the CLI subcommands and Python tools shipped in this repository.

What the tiers mean: free, you get local protection on your own node. Paying, you get continuous review of new patterns, update proposals and explanations — without ever giving up control of your WAF. Inspection and enforcement always run locally; the cloud is only consulted when you opt in, and what it returns is a proposal you approve or discard.

Status: SATGuardian Edge WAF v0.3.0. Detection has been measured on small, hand-written, same-author corpora only. The in-sample rows (100% recall / 0% false positives) are regression floors from corpus/independent_v1.json, not generalization estimates. The current held-out estimate (benchmarks/real_comparative/corpus/heldout_v10.jsonl, run once on 2026-11-08, before any fix) froze the one-shot estimate in heldout_v10_report.json — recall on 70 attacks and 0.0% false positives on 44 controls (95% CI 0.0–8.0%); the current engine measures 100%/0.0% on the same batch as a post-tuning diagnostic, and the earlier heldout_v2 figure (56.1%/7.0%) remains for provenance. No third-party evaluation exists. The benchmark harness compares local Python stand-ins, not vendor products. See STATUS.md and corpus/README.md.

docs.title: 1. ⚙️ WAF Configuration (waf_config.toml & Environment Variables)
docs.text: All local Edge WAF inspection settings are managed declaratively via waf_config.toml in the executable's working directory (or the path given by --config / SATGUARDIAN_CONFIG).

docs.title: 1.1 Core Network & Defense Mode Settings
docs.text:
# Inbound HTTP listener address for protected traffic
listen_addr = "0.0.0.0:8080"

# Target upstream backend application (Nginx, Node, Python, Go, Java, PHP, etc.)
upstream_url = "http://127.0.0.1:3000"

# Defense mode:
#   "block"   - Detected requests are rejected with HTTP 403.
#   "monitor" - Dry-run mode: violations are logged to the ledger and traffic passes.
mode = "block"

Transport reality: the data-plane listener speaks plain HTTP. This build does not terminate TLS and does not support WebSocket; put nginx, Envoy or your existing load balancer in front for TLS termination and keep the WAF on a private hop. upstream_url may be http:// or https:// (the scheme is validated at startup) and calls to the SATGuardian cloud endpoint go out over HTTPS — but nothing in this build serves HTTPS to clients.

docs.title: 1.2 Anti-Reconnaissance Protection (Stealth Mode)
docs.text:
# true  -> Emits a clean web-standard 403 Forbidden without leaking rules, proof, or technology stacks.
# false -> Emits verbose diagnostic JSON containing the causal trace (debug mode).
stealth_mode = true

# Optional custom HTML or text response body when stealth_mode = true
# stealth_block_body = "<html><head><title>403 Forbidden</title></head><body><h1>403 Forbidden</h1></body></html>"

Blocked responses are generic in stealth mode. Per request you can override the behaviour from the command line: satguardian-waf proxy --verbose emits the diagnostic JSON, --stealth forces the generic response.

docs.title: 1.3 Management API & Request Limits
docs.text:
# Dedicated listener for /api/waf/*. It is never mounted on the public data-plane port.
# Set to "off" to disable the management API entirely.
admin_listen_addr = "127.0.0.1:10001"

# Bearer token required by every management route. Prefer SATGUARDIAN_ADMIN_TOKEN
# in the environment over storing it here.
# admin_token = "change-me"

# Maximum accepted inbound request body (2 MiB).
max_body_bytes = 2097152

# IPs or CIDR ranges of upstream proxies allowed to supply X-Forwarded-For /
# X-Real-IP / CF-Connecting-IP / True-Client-IP. Loopback is always trusted.
trusted_proxies = []
  • Every /api/waf/* route requires the admin token; with no token set the routes answer 503 management_api_disabled instead of running unauthenticated. /health and /livez stay open on that listener.
  • Request bodies are capped at max_body_bytes (2 MiB by default).
  • The listener is loopback by default. If you must reach it from another host, put a TLS-terminating reverse proxy with its own authentication in front — the management API itself is plain HTTP.

docs.title: 1.4 Cloud Review Service (Security Units - SU) & SQLite Ledger
docs.text:
Boolean minimization is server-side. This repository ships the edge client only: it normalizes a request into a 128-bit FeatureVector (u128), evaluates compiled clauses locally, and — when you opt in — posts minterms to the SATGuardian cloud synthesis endpoint and stores the returned equation as proposals. No minimizer lives in this code base or in the client binary.

# SATGuardian cloud endpoint for Boolean rule synthesis.
satguardian_api_url = "https://satguardian.tech/api/simplify"

# Cloud API key (or set SATGUARDIAN_API_KEY in the environment).
# satguardian_api_key = "ek_live_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"

# SQLite WAL ledger: audit log plus the table that holds update proposals.
database_path = "waf_ledger.db"

# Seconds between background cloud review runs. Only used when auto_sync_enabled is on.
autonomous_sync_interval_secs = 300

# Send anomalies to the cloud on that timer. Off by default. Turning it on does not
# change the WAF: results are stored as proposals and have to be approved with
# `satguardian-waf clauses apply` or POST /api/waf/clauses/{id}/apply.
auto_sync_enabled = false

What leaves the node, and only if you opt in: the u128 feature vectors recorded as novel anomalies (patterns awaiting analysis). Raw traffic, headers, bodies and client IPs are not uploaded. Everything else — inspection, blocking, rate limiting, the ledger — stays on your node.

Quota behavior: cloud synthesis is metered in Security Units (SU). If the balance is exhausted the cloud call fails and the Edge WAF keeps enforcing the last rule matrix you approved; local inspection is unaffected.

docs.title: 1.5 Layer-7 Stateful & Behavioral Defense (Rate Limiting & Anti-Brute Force)
docs.text:
# Enable temporal sliding window ring buffer analysis
stateful_enabled = true

# Max total requests permitted in sliding window per IP across all endpoints
stateful_global_limit = 300

# Max attempts permitted on sensitive authentication endpoints (/login, /auth, etc.)
stateful_auth_limit = 20

# Sliding temporal window duration in seconds (default: 60s ring buffer)
stateful_window_secs = 60

# Temporary isolation quarantine / jail duration in seconds for offenders (180s)
stateful_ban_secs = 180

# Optional Redis connection URL for distributed cluster state synchronization
# redis_url = "redis://127.0.0.1:6379"

docs.title: 1.6 Envoy Proxy Ext_Authz Integration
docs.text:
# Inbound HTTP listener for Envoy's envoy.filters.http.ext_authz filter
envoy_ext_authz_addr = "0.0.0.0:9002"

The check service speaks the HTTP form of ext_authz (it reads x-envoy-original-method and x-envoy-original-path); the gRPC ext_authz protocol is not implemented in this build. See ENVOY_INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md.

docs.text:
Variable Effect SATGUARDIAN_CONFIG Path to the configuration TOML file. SATGUARDIAN_API_KEY Cloud API key for SATGuardian cloud synthesis (SU metering). SATGUARDIAN_ADMIN_TOKEN (or WAF_ADMIN_TOKEN) Bearer token for every management API route. Without it the routes answer 503. RUST_LOG Tracing verbosity (e.g. RUST_LOG=info or RUST_LOG=satguardian_waf=debug).
